updates.title: Work order part lookup no longer offers a part once it is inactive
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.

Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WOLOOK-01), with description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL WOLOOK PART A), is tracked at {Location-A} with 4 in its default bin and is inactive.
Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) at {Location-A} is open and has an approved line, {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL WOLOOK line"), that holds no parts.
Before {Part-A} was set inactive, typing the start of its number in that line's part lookup offered it.
steps: Open {Work-order-1} and go to its Lines tab.
On {Line-1} open the line's ⋮ menu and click "Request part".
In the "New Part Request" dialog type the start of {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WOL) in Part Number.
Clear Part Number and type {Description-A}.
Close the dialog with ×.
results: Step 2: The "New Part Request" dialog opens.
Step 3: No row for {Part-A} is offered: no inventory row with "Inventory Qty" and no "Part Library" row. If nothing else matches, the list reads "No results".
Step 4: Again no row for {Part-A} is offered.
Step 5: The dialog closes and {Line-1} still holds no parts.
updates.source: Epic SV-10647; story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S9-R1, S9-E10, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas boards 6.1 (While active: GREASETUBE is found) and 6.2 (Once inactive: not offered), 13 Oct copy. Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan", 7 Oct 2026 (informs, never overrules), §6 Phase 7; SV-10822 acceptance criteria (the PRD wins where they differ). Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).
quotes: S9-R1
Part lookup on a work order line does not return inactive parts.

If ShopView adds a way to raise a part request from a purchase order, it uses the purchase order's part lookup, which leaves inactive parts out (S9-R5). Today part requests are raised on the work order (S9-R1).
SV-10822 acceptance criteria

Given GREASETUBE is inactive, when the user searches "GREASE" on a work order, estimate, part sale, purchase order or technician charge-out, then it is not offered, neither as an inventory part nor as a Part Library entry.
Tech plan (Parts Lifecycle Update, 7 Oct 2026), §6 Phase 7, ListingQueryHandler
Covers WO, estimate, tech charge-out (every device), PO, vendor-bill re-point, part sale

doc_part1: Sign in as an Admin (or Owner) and pick the location in the top-bar location switcher (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). This location is {Location-A}; every step runs there unless it names another location.

Go to Parts → Inventory and click "New Inventory Part". Type Description (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL WOLOOK PART A) and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WOLOOK-01). The part number you typed is {Part-A} and the description is {Description-A}.

Pick Category (for example Uncategorized), type Cost (for example 10.00) and Sell Price (for example 20.00), leave "Track quantities and cost of goods" on, set the default bin's Quantity to 4 and click Save.

Go to Work Orders and click "New Work Order". In Customer click Add and create a customer (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL WOLOOK Customer"); in Asset click Add and create a unit (for example "ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WOLOOK-UNIT"); click Create. The number shown at the top left (for example S2-15440) is {Work-order-1}.
On {Work-order-1} click "New Line", type Title (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL WOLOOK line") and click "Save & Close". This line is {Line-1}. Click "Approve" on {Line-1}.

While {Part-A} is still active, on {Line-1} open the ⋮ menu, click "Request part" and type the start of {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-WOL) in Part Number: {Part-A} is offered with "Inventory Qty: 4". Close the dialog with × without saving.

Set {Part-A} inactive: on Parts → Inventory, Active tab, search {Part-A}, click its row, pick Part Status "Inactive", click Save, leave "Note (Optional)" empty and click "Deactivate" in the "Deactivate part?" confirmation.

Check the setup worked: on Parts → Inventory the Inactive tab lists {Part-A} and the Active tab does not, and {Line-1} on {Work-order-1} holds no parts. If {Part-A} is still on the Active tab, repeat the previous item.
doc_part2: Fastest reliable route: drive Part 1 in the browser with Playwright, using the labels in Part 1; no request shape below has been observed on a Part Lifecycle build.

UNVERIFIED: after release a new part is created with POST /api/inventory/parts/create carrying partNumber, description and isTracked instead of catalogPartId (tech plan §5). Record the request the dialog sends and reuse it for further parts.
{Part-A id} = the id of {Part-A}: read it from GET /api/inventory/parts?search=<the part number> (playbook §E) and record it.

UNVERIFIED: a status change is sent as PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with partIds, status ("active" or "inactive") and note (tech plan §5), for the dialog and the bulk bar alike. Record what the confirmation sends.

Work orders: the playbook (§D, Navigation Map) says a freshly created work order reliably opens its detail page while an existing one can bounce to /workorders, so create the work order fresh and stay on it; lines are made with the New Line dialog (POST /api/work-orders/lines/create needs a canned line).

UNVERIFIED: the line lookup reads GET /api/work-orders/part/request/inventory-parts-as-options-with-remaining-catalogue-parts, which after release leaves out inactive parts and adds inactiveMatch (tech plan §5). Judge only from the dropdown on screen; keep the response as extra evidence.
Trap: wait for the dropdown to settle before reading it. The check in Part 1 while the part was active proves the search reaches {Part-A}, so an empty list afterwards is a real result.
Evidence: take a screenshot at every step that has an expected result, and record the build marker before you start.

updates.title: A work order line keeps its inactive part and can still be edited
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-KEEPLINE-01) is tracked at {Location-A}, has Sell Price $20.00 and 4 in its default bin.
Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open and its approved line {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL KEEPLINE line") holds {Part-A} with quantity 2, added while {Part-A} was active.
{Part-A} was set inactive after it was added to {Line-1}.
steps: Open {Work-order-1} and read the {Part-A} row on {Line-1}.
Open the {Part-A} row, change Quantity from 2 to 3 and save.
Open the row again, change Sell Price to $22.00 and save.
Open the row again, add the note "ZZAUTOTEST still here" and save.
results: Step 1: The row is still on {Line-1}: quantity 2, $20.00, total $40.00 (2 × $20.00).
Step 2: The change saves and the row total reads $60.00 (3 × $20.00).
Step 3: The change saves and the row total reads $66.00 (3 × $22.00); the line total includes it.
Step 4: The note saves and the row still holds {Part-A}.

{Part-A} was set inactive after the invoice was created.

Open the Finance tab and read the invoice.

Step 2: The invoice shows {Part-A}, 1 × $20.00.
Step 3: The print preview opens and lists {Part-A}.
Step 4: The report lists {Part-A} with a sold quantity of 1.

updates.title: Technician charge-out does not offer or accept an inactive part
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
{Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL TECHDESK) is a staff member at {Location-A} with the default Technician role, signed in in a second browser on a desktop computer.

Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TECHDESK-01), with description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL TECHDESK PART A), is tracked at {Location-A} with 4 in its default bin and is inactive.
Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open and has an approved line, {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST PL TECHDESK line"), with {Technician-A} as a technician and no parts.
steps: As {Technician-A}, open {Work-order-1}.
Under {Line-1} click "+ Add Part".
In the new part row type the start of {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TECHD) in the part field.
Clear the field and type {Part-A} in full, all in lower case.
Press Enter (or click the row's "Save").
results: Step 3: No row for {Part-A} is offered.

Step 4: The field shows, as its error, "{Part-A} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.", with {Part-A} written as it was saved (capitals and hyphens). No offer to add it as a special order or a new part appears.
Step 5: The row is not saved: {Line-1} gets no new part and the error stays under the field.

updates.title: Bulk change that partly fails lists the failed part and its reason
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PARTFAIL-01) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.

{Part-A} and {Part-B} share the start of their numbers (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PARTFAIL-0), so one search lists them together.
A second browser tab is open on Parts → Inventory at {Location-A}.
steps: In the first tab, on the Active tab, search the start that {Part-A} and {Part-B} share (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PARTFAIL-0).
Open the ⋮ actions menu and click "Deactivate parts".
Tick {Part-A} and {Part-B}.
In the second tab open {Part-B}, pick Part Status "Inactive", click Save and click "Deactivate".
In the first tab click "Deactivate" in the bulk bar, then "Deactivate" in the confirmation.
Read the message at the bottom right.
Wait 10 seconds. Do not close the message.
results: Step 5: {Part-A} leaves the Active tab; the bulk mode stays on with only {Part-B} ticked (2 ticked = 1 changed + 1 failed).
Step 6: An error message reads "1 part updated, 1 could not be changed." and lists {Part-B} by its part number with the reason "Part is already in that state."

For each part that failed, the system names the part by its number and gives the reason.
The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."
PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (A part already in the requested state)
"Part is already in that state." | Listed as the failure reason

updates.title: Bulk change of forty parts writes forty Part History entries
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.

Forty inventory parts, {Part-A} to {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BULK40-01 to ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BULK40-40), are tracked and active at {Location-A}, and no other part's number starts with ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BULK40.
steps: On the Active tab search "ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BULK40" and scroll to the bottom so all 40 rows are loaded.
Turn on "Deactivate parts" and tick the header checkbox.
Click "Deactivate", type the note "ZZAUTOTEST bulk forty" and confirm with "Deactivate".
Open the Inactive tab and search "ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BULK40".
Open the Part History of each of the 40 parts in turn, ticking each off on a list.
results: Step 2: The bulk bar reads 40 selected.
Step 3: "40 parts updated." shows.
Step 4: 40 rows are listed (30, then 10 more after scrolling).
Step 5: Each of the 40 parts has exactly one new entry "Deactivated | Reason: ZZAUTOTEST bulk forty": 40 parts × 1 entry = 40 entries, all with the same note.

steps: On the Active tab search the shared start (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-BCORE-0).

notes: Coverage: every S9 and S10 code is quoted by a case in this file except S9-E9 (public API refuses a duplicate create) and S10-R25a ("| Changed through: Public API"). Both are public-API only and are held by share A's cases C425755 and C425776 in section 54275 "Retire OR retest"; they are listed in anchors_covered against those cases. If share A retires either case, the code needs a new home.

S9-R4 and S9-R7 describe screens ShopView does not have (PRD Story 9 context note; tech plan §10 marks them N/A). New case D-02 checks that no invoice-line or scan lookup exists and, if one has appeared, that it leaves out an inactive part.
Retire C425759 (Dashboard Critical Reorder list leaves out an inactive part): S9-E12 was removed in v27; Product answer 13 says drop those tests.

Design vs PRD, board numbering: the canned-job warning is board 6.5 "The canned job leaves it out" (file daily-05-p6-2-canned-warning); the task text calls it 6.2. In the 13 Oct copy it reads "These parts are inactive and were not added: GREASETUBE.", which matches S9-R10 and S9-R10b. Resolved. Board 6.2 is "Once inactive: not offered" (No results).

Design (example data only): board 6.5 now shows the canned job added twice (Lines (4), lines 3 and 4 both "Replace - Steering shaft u joints", two parts each) while board 6.4 shows "Lines (2)". No effect on any expected result.

Design vs PRD, board 2.6 (Part History at Lethbridge): the 13 Oct html text keeps production column widths and the canvas note says the build still narrows Staff/Date/Time and needs fixing, but the PNG image is unchanged and still shows narrowed Staff/Date/Time columns. C154798 follows S10-R21 (columns keep their layout).

Design: boards 6.6 and 6.7 place the grey Inactive pill beside the description (vendor return) and after the part number (credit), matching S9-R12 and S9-R13. No board shows a purchase order lookup, vendor bill re-point, part sale lookup, technician charge-out (desktop or phone), global search, a failed bulk change, a core, the forty-part change, Min/Max entries, bin-split history entries or price search; those cases follow the PRD only.

Story vs PRD: SV-10822 and SV-10823 match PRD v27 for Stories 9 and 10 (S9-R10b and S10-R12a present, S9-E12 absent). The verification ticket SV-11041 still lists S9-E12 and the check "Dashboard Critical Reorder leaves out untracked and inactive parts (S5-R14, S9-E12)"; the PRD removed both (Product answer 13), so the PRD wins.

Tech plan vs PRD: the tech plan (7 Oct, written against PRD v22) still plans the Critical Reorder filter for S9-E12 (§6 Phase 4, fetchCriticalReorder) and lists S9-E12 in its traceability; removed in v27. It also builds the canned-job warning from the skipped part number without saying whose number (written before S9-R10b): C425731 checks that the warning names the inventory part's own number, not the typed one.

Question for Product (no quotable source): S10-R8 gives "This part ..." for one part on bulk reactivation but keeps "Existing records that use them stay as they are.", while S10-R5 switches to "use it" for one part on deactivation. C425762 and C425763 follow the PRD's words ("use them"). Was "use it" intended for one part?

Question for Product (no quotable source): S9-R10 does not say in what order, or with what separator, the part numbers are listed in the canned-job warning. C425730 accepts either order of the two numbers (the tech plan says ", " in canned-job order, which informs only).

Question (no quotable source): the PRD does not say whether a core has a row of its own on the Inventory list, where it could be ticked (S10-R13a, S2-N3) or have its Part History opened (S10-R19, S10-R26). The QA lead's 9 Oct set-up answer says cores show in the Inventory list's "Core" column and as "Core for <part>" rows on Parts → Returns. C425766, C425769 and C425777 therefore record whether a core row exists and say 'not checked by hand' if it does not.

Question (no quotable source): which permissions let a role create a vendor return without 'Part Library & Inventory → View' (needed by C425746, S9-N3). The setup doc marks it UNVERIFIED.
